title: Tensor constructibility for admissible coefficients
statement: Let ell be prime and k a positive-characteristic field of characteristic different from ell. Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring satisfying IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ell Lambda. Let the schemes and morphisms be separated of finite type over k. For any K and M on X which are constant-model bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude, their specified relative derived tensor is constant-model bounded constructible. No Tor-amplitude conclusion is asserted here.

proof.text: For finite $A$, descend $K,L\in\Dctf(X,A)$ to the étale site by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]; $A$ is Noetherian because every ideal is a finite set. Choose ordered Tor intervals $[a,b]$, $[c,d]$. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], represent the descended objects by bounded complexes $P,Q$ of flat constructible sheaves, zero outside these intervals. Refine the finitely many stratifications of their terms by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection]. On each stratum, [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor], applied to the flat terms in degree zero, shows that $P^i\otimes_AQ^j$ is locally constant of finite type. Finite sums and the kernels and cokernels computing cohomology are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. Each tensor term is flat: tensoring with $P^i\otimes_AQ^j$ is the composite of two exact tensor functors; finite sums remain exact. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_AQ)$ is a bounded flat complex, supported in $[a+c,b+d]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], so it computes the derived tensor and has this Tor interval against every module sheaf. The monoidal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies its exact pro-étale pullback with $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$. The Tor comparison equivalence gives the finite-coefficient tensor assertion of (1).

proof.text: For $\mathcal O_E$, [det-lem-integral-models-operations](2) gives tensor closure of $\Dbc$. For $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [det-thm-sf-pf-field-tensor](1) gives tensor closure of $\Dbc$. proof.text:
1. Finite type over the field makes X Noetherian and qcqs. Transport along the ring-object
isomorphism in hΛ; scalar restriction along an isomorphism is an exact monoidal equivalence,
preserves finite constant presentations, and hence preserves the two constructibility
predicates and Tor intervals.
2. For a finite ring A, use finiteTorComparisonNoetherian to descend both complexes with
unchanged Tor intervals to the etale site. The finite-value flat-constructible-model theorem
represents them by bounded flat constructible complexes in those intervals. Refine the
finitely many termwise stratifications. Tensor terms are constructible on the refinement:
locally they are tensors of finite A-modules, and these are finite. Finite direct sums,
kernels and cokernels remain constructible. The total tensor is bounded, has these
constructible cohomology sheaves, and is K-flat since it is bounded with flat terms. The
monoidal comparison pullback identifies it with the specified pro-etale derived tensor.
3. For O_E apply integralModelsOperations(2); for E and the finite-subextension-valued
algebraic closure apply tensorClosureRational(1). The base-field cases Z_l and Q_l are
O_E and E at E = Q_l. For the retained all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficient,
apply the lisse-generator argument directly: finite presented scalar modules over the
field are finite free; after refining the stratifications the tensor of the two lisse
factors is lisse finite free. The locally closed projection formula and finite-cone
induction give constructibility, as in the proof of tensorClosureRational. This keeps the all-continuous coefficient distinct
from the finite-subextension-valued one. Transport back through the isomorphism of step 1.
The zero ring, zero complexes and empty strata are included by the same constructions.
